# Rule catalog

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:gen`. Do not edit by hand. -->

18 rules. "Verified on" is the date the message format was checked against real tool output; "not verified" means the format comes from documentation or knowledge of the tool and has not been checked against a real run, so treat matches with extra care.

Fixtures for every rule are synthetic and written by hand; passing them does not measure accuracy on real logs.

## Source notes

### `generic.exit-code`

Line "##[error]Process completed with exit code N." observed in a real GitHub Actions log.

### `github.token-permissions`

GitHub API error message "Resource not accessible by integration"; not checked against a real run in this project.

### `infra.disk-full`

POSIX/Node.js message "ENOSPC: no space left on device" / "No space left on device"; not checked against a real run in this project. The inotify variant (ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached) is deliberately excluded.

### `infra.oom.node-heap`

V8 fatal error text "JavaScript heap out of memory"; not checked against a real run in this project.

### `node.eslint.problems`

Checked against real ESLint 10.12.0 default ("stylish") formatter output. Other formatters are not covered.

### `node.module-not-found`

Checked against real Node 22 output for require() and import of a missing package. The Jest variant ("Cannot find module ... from ...") was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `node.npm.auth`

Message format "npm error code E401|E403" follows the same prefix as the verified E404 output; the exact wording of the following lines was not checked against a real registry response.

### `node.npm.ci-lock-mismatch`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm ci with a modified package.json, and npm ci without a lockfile).

### `node.npm.e404`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm install of a non-existent package).

### `node.npm.eacces`

EACCES is a Node.js/POSIX error code; the surrounding npm message format was not checked against a real run.

### `node.npm.eresolve`

Checked against real npm 10.9.0 output (npm install with conflicting peer dependencies).

### `node.prettier.check`

Checked against real Prettier 3.9.10 output of "prettier --check".

### `node.test.failures`

Vitest 5.0.4 output checked against a real run. The Jest output format ("FAIL file", "Tests: N failed") follows Jest documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.test.snapshot`

Vitest 5.0.4 "Snapshot `name` mismatched" checked against a real run. Jest wording ("Snapshot name:", "Snapshots: N failed") follows Jest documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.test.timeout`

Vitest 5.0.4 "Test timed out in Nms." checked against a real run. Jest ("Exceeded timeout of N ms for a test") and Mocha ("Timeout of Nms exceeded.") wording follows their documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `node.typescript.errors`

Checked against real tsc 6.0.3 output ("file(line,col): error TSxxxx: message"). The "--pretty" variant ("file:line:col - error TSxxxx") follows the TypeScript documentation and was not checked against a real run.

### `python.import-error`

ModuleNotFoundError checked against real pytest 9.1.1 output on Python 3.14. The "ImportError: cannot import name" wording was not checked against a real run, so it is reported with medium confidence.

### `python.pytest.failures`

Checked against real pytest 9.1.1 output (short test summary and final summary line).
